_note: Worked example: the 'Set for you' stall on mpaiva.com, before and after the fix (mpaiva/jupiter 0249bbb). The voice is picked by ear at the script gate; af_heart is the default until then.

lines.b-intro: This is the home page of [Marcelo](/mɑɹsˈɛloʊ/) [Paiva's](/pˈaɪvəz/) site, in Safari, with VoiceOver on. I'm going to listen to it the way someone who can't see the screen would meet it.
lines.b-goal: The goal of this test is simple. Can someone using VoiceOver understand this page, find what they need, and use its controls, without seeing it?
lines.b-steps: I test in six steps. First, I inspect the page structure in the code. Second, the keyboard on its own. Third, a reading pass with the screen reader, top to bottom. Fourth, jumping by headings, landmarks and links. Fifth, the controls themselves. And sixth, real tasks, start to finish.
lines.b-scope: Steps one and two come before the screen reader. In this video I'm on step three, the reading pass… and step five, the settings control.
lines.b-skip: The first thing it reaches is a skip link, which is a good start. That's [WCAG](/wˈʌkæɡ/) two point four point one, Bypass Blocks. Now I'll read the header one item at a time.
lines.b-setforyou: Set for you… a button, and it tells me it's collapsed. That's what [WCAG](/wˈʌkæɡ/) four point one point two asks for: a name, a role, and a state. Next item.
lines.b-menu: It says menu… and again… and again. Four presses, and it hasn't moved past it.
lines.b-why: There's no menu on screen. The settings panel is closed, but the four dropdowns inside it are still reaching VoiceOver. That's a problem under [WCAG](/wˈʌkæɡ/) four point one point two, Name, Role, Value: VoiceOver is handed a menu with no name, for something that isn't there. If you're listening, it sounds like the page has stopped, right at the control that sets the site up for you.
lines.a-fix: The fix is to leave the panel empty while it's closed. Here's the same page after that change. I'll go straight to Set for you.
lines.a-next: Collapsed, the same as before. Next item.
lines.a-pause: That's Pause motion, the next button on the screen. The silence is gone, and four point one point two holds here.
lines.a-open: And when I open it, the first setting reads out its name and its value… Drawings, in calm color.
lines.a-close: Same panel, same settings… it just stopped announcing things that aren't on screen.
lines.v3-open: Step three, the reading pass. The home page from the top, in Safari with VoiceOver, the way someone who can't see the screen would meet it.
lines.v7-open: Fix and re-test. The panel is now left empty while it's closed. I'll go straight to Set for you.
lines.v0-series: In this series, each step gets its own short video, on this same page. Along the way I find a problem in one of its controls… and the last video shows it fixed, and tested again.
lines.v4-open: Step four, structural navigation. Someone using a screen reader rarely reads every item. They jump, by headings, by landmarks, and by links. First, headings.
lines.v4-headings: One level one, a level two for the latest writing, and the essays under it at level three. The outline holds, all the way down. That's [WCAG](/wˈʌkæɡ/) one point three point one, Info and Relationships.
lines.v4-landmarks-ok: Each region is announced with a name, so I can tell them apart and jump straight to the one I want.
lines.v4-links: And links. In a list of links, each one has to make sense on its own.
lines.v4-doubled: Here's a problem. The essays in the drawing strip read their title twice, and then the whole summary. The purpose is clear, so [WCAG](/wˈʌkæɡ/) two point four point four is met… but a list like this is slow to get through.
lines.v5-open: Step five, the controls. Finding Set for you isn't enough. It has to say what it is, what state it's in, and work from the keyboard.
lines.v5-state: Name, Set for you. Role, button. State, collapsed. That's [WCAG](/wˈʌkæɡ/) four point one point two.
lines.v5-expanded: When I press it, the state changes to expanded, and VoiceOver says so. Now the panel, one item at a time.
lines.v5-selects: The settings read as a sentence, and each dropdown has its own name… Drawings, Theme, Motion, Home page… with its current value first.
lines.v5-escape: And Escape closes it, and puts me back on the button, collapsed again. Focus isn't lost.
lines.v6-open: Step six, a real task. I'll turn the drawings off, start to finish, with VoiceOver… and find out whether it tells me it worked.
lines.v6-found: There's the Drawings dropdown, set to calm color. I'll open it, and choose not at all.
lines.v6-stale: When I choose it, VoiceOver reads the old value… calm color. That seems to be VoiceOver in Safari with a standard dropdown. I have to ask again to hear what's set.
lines.v6-silent: Not at all. It worked… but nothing told me. The panel has a note about it, so I'll go and find it.
lines.v6-note: There it is. Drawings are off, and their captions go with them. That's a status message, and it's only on screen: it should be announced without me going to look. That's a problem under [WCAG](/wˈʌkæɡ/) four point one point three, Status Messages.
lines.v6-gone: And after See the work, VoiceOver goes straight to Latest writing. The drawings are gone for a listener too. The task works… it just doesn't say so.
lines.v6b-open: Since then, the panel says what a change did. Here's the same task on the fixed version, the one that's live now.
lines.v6b-heard: There it is. Drawings are off, and their captions go with them. It still reads the old value first… but now the result is spoken, without going to look. [WCAG](/wˈʌkæɡ/) four point one point three holds here.
lines.v2-open: Step two, the keyboard on its own. No screen reader and no mouse, just the keys a keyboard user presses, and the focus ring that shows where I am.
lines.v2-skip: The first stop is a skip link. I'll press Return, then Tab, to see whether it really skips the header.
lines.v2-skipped: I'm on Read the writing, past the whole header. The skip link works. Now back up, with Shift-Tab.
lines.v2-order: Pause motion, then Set for you: the same order as on screen, and the focus ring follows every time. That's [WCAG](/wˈʌkæɡ/) two point four point seven, Focus Visible. I'll open it with Return.
lines.v2-panel: It opens, and Tab moves through each setting, by name. Now Escape.
lines.v2-escape: Escape closes it, and puts focus back on the button. Focus isn't trapped, and it isn't lost. [WCAG](/wˈʌkæɡ/) two point one point one, Keyboard, holds here.
lines.v1-open: Step one, before any screen reader: the structure in the code. I'm opening Safari's Web Inspector, and making it larger, to see what this page tells assistive technology.
lines.v1-button: This is the Set for you button. Its attributes say aria-expanded, false, so it's announced as collapsed… and aria-controls points at the panel it opens. That's what I want to see.
lines.v1-count: That panel is marked hidden, and the four dropdowns are still inside it, in the page. Hidden content should stay out of a screen reader's way… so that's the first thing I'll listen for, in the reading pass.
lines.v2-type: It opens, and Tab takes me to the first setting, the drawings. With a dropdown focused, I can type the first letter of a choice. N, for not at all.
lines.v2-changed: The dropdown says not at all, and the drawings are gone. The setting changed without a mouse. Now Escape.
lines.v2-escape2: Escape closes the panel, and puts focus back on the button. Focus isn't trapped, and it isn't lost. Next, Pause motion.
lines.v2-pause: Space presses it, and the button now says pressed.
lines.v2-close: Tab, Shift-Tab, Return, Escape, Space, and typing to choose. Every control I used works without a mouse, and the focus ring showed me where I was each time. For what I tested, the goal of step two is met. [WCAG](/wˈʌkæɡ/) two point one point one, Keyboard, holds here.
lines.v8-open: One more feature to test: Describe this page. A screen reader reads a page one item at a time, in a line. It doesn't say that the essays fill most of the page, or that a narrow column sits beside them. A sighted visitor takes that in at a glance.
lines.v8-why: For someone who's blind, a picture of the layout is a map. It says what's on the page before reading all of it, and where things are when a sighted colleague says it's in the column on the right. This button describes the layout in words.
lines.v8-press: It's the second thing on the page, right after the skip link. I'll press it.
lines.v8-silent: The dialog opened on screen… but VoiceOver didn't say so. Someone listening wouldn't know it's there. I'll move on, to find it.
lines.v8-in: There it is: a dialog called The home page. I'll step into it.
lines.v8-like: This is what the button is for. It starts with a picture: the front page of a magazine, the newest essays taking most of the page, and a narrower column beside them. Then it walks the layout from top to bottom, in order.
lines.v8-close: Escape closes it, and puts me back on the button. What it says is useful. The gap is the opening: VoiceOver in Safari should hear that the dialog appeared. And nobody who relies on a description like this has told me yet whether it helps. That's the next test, with people.
lines.v8-close2: Escape closes it, and puts me back on the button. What it says is useful. The gap is the opening: when the dialog appears, VoiceOver should say so. And nobody who relies on a description like this has told me yet whether it helps. That's the next test, with people.
lines.v9-open: Last, what this first pass can't tell me. A screen reader shows whether things work as built, not whether they help the people they're for. These need people with disabilities, on their own devices and settings.
lines.v9-describe: First, Describe this page. Does a written description of the layout help someone picture the page? Is it too long, or too short? Blind people who use a screen reader every day should tell us, on VoiceOver and on JAWS or NVDA.
lines.v9-readers: Second, other screen readers and devices. This pass used VoiceOver in Safari only, and its biggest finding came from how Safari passes hidden content to VoiceOver. JAWS, NVDA, VoiceOver on iPhone and TalkBack all behave differently.
lines.v9-sentence: Third, Set for you reads its settings as a sentence. Whether that feels natural, and whether the new announcements are enough, is for screen reader users, and people with cognitive or learning disabilities, to say.
lines.v9-motion: Fourth, motion. The drawings drift and the background moves. The pause button works… but is it found in time, and is the motion comfortable before it is? People with vestibular disorders can tell us.
lines.v9-zoom: Fifth, zoom and magnification. Zoomed in, the header stays at the top, and some text sits over moving colour. People with low vision who use zoom or a screen magnifier should try it.
lines.v9-voice: Sixth, voice control and switch access. Names were checked for what a screen reader says, not for what people say aloud, and the home page has more than fifty stops for someone moving one step at a time.
lines.v9-collage: And last, this dropdown. Set for you can turn the home page into a collage of drawings. This pass tested the list only.
lines.v9-close: That's the end of the first pass. Five problems found on the page: three fixed and live, one fix in review, and one still open. The next test is with people.
lines.v9-collage2: And last, the collage. Set for you can turn the home page into a field of drawings. This pass tested the list only.
